## What was done

Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVPrinterAgentTest.java` — the only file added/changed.

**Style matched to the existing suite** (`CSVParserTest`, `CSVFormatTest`, `CSVRecordTest`): JUnit 4.11, static `org.junit.Assert.*` imports, `@Test` / `@Test(expected = …)`, `static org.apache.commons.csv.Constants.CRLF`, Java-1.5-compatible source (explicit generics, no `@Override` on interface methods).

**Coverage of the public API:**

| Area | Cases |
|---|---|
| Constructor | null `out` → `IllegalArgumentException`; null `format` → `IllegalArgumentException`; inconsistent format (quoteChar == delimiter) → `IllegalStateException`; no header → empty output; supplied header printed & quoted; empty `withHeader()` → lone record separator |
| `getOut()` | returns the same `Appendable` instance |
| `print(Object)` | plain value unquoted; non-String via `toString()`; delimiter/quote/newline/leading-space/trailing-space trigger quoting; quote char doubled; `null` → empty vs. configured null-string; second value separated by delimiter |
| `println()` | writes record separator; null record separator writes nothing; resets new-record state (no leading delimiter) |
| `printRecord(Object…/Iterable)` | varargs, iterable, empty record, multiple records, empty-leading-value quoted but empty-trailing-value not |
| `printRecords(Object[]/Iterable/ResultSet)` | array-of-arrays, flat array (one value per record), iterable-of-iterables, iterable of plain values, mixed elements, and a real JDBC `ResultSet` via in-memory H2 |
| `printComment` | no-op (incl. `null`) when commenting disabled; single line; multi-line with `\n` and with `\r\n` (single break); forces newline after a value; `null` → `NullPointerException` when commenting enabled |
| Quote policies | `ALL`, `NON_NUMERIC` (numbers unquoted), `NONE` (escapes instead) |
| Escaping | delimiter + newline escaping; `CSVFormat.MYSQL` (tab + backslash) |
| Round trip | parse → `printRecord(CSVRecord)` reproduces the input |
| `close()` / `flush()` | forwarded to a `Closeable`/`Flushable` appendable (tracked); no-op for `StringBuilder` without corrupting output; `flush()` pushes buffered bytes through a `BufferedWriter` to the underlying `StringWriter` (observable state) |

Every test asserts on the exact written text or on observable state (flushed/closed flags, `StringWriter` contents through a buffer), not merely absence of exceptions.
